record.original_question: For every compact analytic two-dimensional Riemannian manifold M with analytic boundary, is the set GM(M) of generalized minimal flows a nonempty proper subset of the Yudovich space YU(M), where YU(M) consists of divergence-free vector fields with bounded vorticity?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a compact two-dimensional real-analytic Riemannian manifold with real-analytic boundary. Define the Yudovich space
$$\mathrm{YU}(M) = \{ u \in L^2(M; TM) : \operatorname{div} u = 0,\ u \cdot \nu|_{\partial M} = 0,\ \operatorname{curl} u \in L^\infty(M)\},$$
i.e., divergence-free, tangent-to-boundary vector fields on $M$ whose vorticity $\omega = \operatorname{curl} u$ is essentially bounded. Within $\mathrm{YU}(M)$, call $u$ a generalized minimal flow if it is a stationary solution of the incompressible Euler equation on $M$ that arises as a weak limit (or, equivalently, as a minimizer in the appropriate variational/relaxed sense) of the energy among isovortical rearrangements—so that $u$ minimizes the kinetic energy $\tfrac12\int_M |u|^2$ within its generalized vorticity class. Let $\mathrm{GM}(M) \subset \mathrm{YU}(M)$ denote the set of all such generalized minimal flows on $M$.

Prove that for every such $M$, the set $\mathrm{GM}(M)$ is a nonempty proper subset of $\mathrm{YU}(M)$:
$$\varnothing \neq \mathrm{GM}(M) \subsetneq \mathrm{YU}(M).$$
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem in the surveys on geometric hydrodynamics; the search returned no proof establishing nonemptiness and properness of GM(M) inside the Yudovich space YU(M) for all compact analytic surfaces with analytic boundary. It is listed among current open problems on generalized minimal flows.

status_evidence.title: Geometry of generalized fluid flows
status_evidence.snippet: Studies of generalized fluid flows on Riemannian manifolds; no proof of the GM(M) ⊊ YU(M) non-trivial inclusion for all compact analytic surfaces is given.
status_evidence.claim: Related literature does not provide a complete resolution of the problem.
